short: The decisive final battle where Alexander the Great destroyed the army of Darius III and conquered the Persian Empire.
full:
On 1 October 331 BCE, on the plains of Gaugamela near the Tigris River, Alexander the Great faced the massive rebuilt army of the Persian King Darius III. Darius had chosen flat, open ground to maximize his vast numerical advantage and deploy scythed chariots. Alexander countered with a complex tactical manoeuvre, shifting his lines diagonally to draw the Persian cavalry away from the center, creating a gap in the enemy formation.

Alexander personally led a wedge formation of his companion cavalry straight into this gap, directly targeting the Persian king. For the second time, Darius fled the battlefield, causing his army's morale to collapse. The decisive Macedonian victory effectively ended the Achaemenid Persian Empire and left Alexander as the undisputed ruler of western Asia.
